sections.title: Clinical Pearls & Management Algorithms
sections.content:
• Optic atrophy may be unilateral or bilateral. • Optic atrophy may be congenital or acquired. • Optic atrophy may be primary, secondary or consecutive.

[CAUSES]
Primary: optic neuritis, optic n compression by tumour, aneurysm, hereditary optic neuropathy, toxic and nutritional optic neuropathy.
Secondary: chronic papilledema, AION, papillitis, ocular inflammatory causes of disc swelling.
Consecutive: diseases of inner retina and its blood supply, extensive retinal photocoagulation, retinitis pigmentosa, previous central retinal a occlusion.
Glaucomatous: primary or secondary glaucoma, congenital or acquired glaucoma.

branches: Risks: Age, Pregnancy, Synthetic estrogen, Trauma, Surgery, Past DVT, Cancer, Obesity, Immobility, Thrombophilia
Signs: Calf warmth, Tenderness, Swelling, Erythema, Fever, Pitting edema
Prevention: Stop OCP 4w pre-op, Early mobilization, LMWH (Enoxaparin 20mg), Compression stockings, Pneumatic devices

sections.title: Anaphylaxis Management
content: 1. Secure airway, O2, intubate if needed.

sections.title: Endocrine & Emergency Protocols
sections.content:
DKA MANAGEMENT: 1. ABC, 2. Two large bore cannulae, 3. Fluid resuscitation, 4. VBG/Glucose/Labs, 5. Insulin infusion 0.1unit/kg/h, 6. Monitor ketones hourly, 7. Start LMWH, 8. 10% glucose when glucose <14mmol/L to avoid hypoglycemia. 

HYPOGLYCEMIA: 15-20g quick acting carb, or IV glucose 10% 200ml/15min, or Glucagon 1mg.

HHS: Rehydrate slowly over 48h, replace K+, insulin only if blood glucose not falling or ketonaemia exists.
